clue.text: Vessel settled — on board, crew starts to bail out

indicators.note: something on board is held within, so the crew and the starts sit inside the word for settled

parts.note: settled, as in sat down, gives SAT
a crew is a team

indicators.note: the starts of the words bail and out are their first letters

explanation.surface: A boat has settled low in the water, and the crew begin bailing it out.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam-powered boat is a kind of vessel, the general word for a ship or craft.

clue.text: Place its said for great deal?

indicators.note: said means the word for place is to be pronounced, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: a place is a site

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a place counts as a great bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: The informal sense is the one in 'a sight better', meaning by a great deal. The clue's 'its' stands for 'it's'.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal use the word means a lot, as in 'a sight more expensive' or 'a sight too clever'.

clue.text: Wanting the best position in race after turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the built word from bottom to top, so backwards
the word for position goes inside the word for race

parts.note: a mile is a race over that distance
to sit, as for a portrait, is to take a position or pose

explanation.surface: Someone after a top place in a race only after their form has picked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is only a link word. 'turning up' reverses the whole build, giving the answer from bottom to top; 'sit' in the sense of position is far down the dictionary list.
explanation.definitionFit: The belief that only a select, superior few deserve favour is the attitude of wanting the best.

clue.text: Fine rain and shelter will be limiting to plant

parts.note: fine rain is mist

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the word for shelter holds the word to within it

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Drizzle and a shelter combine to restrict a plant's growth.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a parasitic evergreen with white berries, hung at Christmas for kissing under.

clue.text: How the solver's performance may be judged — ready?

definitions.text: How the solver's performance may be judged
definitions.meaning: a solver's work is graded according to the scores given to it
the starter's call before a race, followed by 'get set, go'

explanation.surface: Whoever tackles this puzzle wonders how they will be graded, and whether they are prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is about scores awarded; as a race-start command it asks runners to get prepared.

clue.text: Surface belly up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a pot is a pot belly, a paunch

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a belly can be the surface when it is turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The uppermost part of something is its surface, as in the top of a table.

clue.text: Turns back, having no time for puzzle

indicators.note: having no means going without, so the letter for time is dropped

parts.note: to rebut is to repel or turn back an attack or argument

explanation.surface: Someone retreats, having no time left for a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A word puzzle in which pictures or symbols stand for syllables or words.

clue.text: Monarch establishing a line?

definitions.meaning: a monarch is a king or queen who governs
a straight edge used for drawing lines, a yardstick

explanation.surface: A king founding a dynasty, a line of succession.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both one who governs and the measuring strip used to draw straight lines.

clue.text: Asian holiday spot entertaining English may be Indian

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the abbreviation for English sits inside the island

parts.note: Bali is an Indonesian island popular with tourists

explanation.surface: An Asian resort playing host to English visitors, who may be Indian.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: someone from West Bengal is Indian, though people from Bangladesh share the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Bengal, much of which lies in India, so such a person may well be an Indian.

clue.text: Identify indefinite number in view when men behave badly?

indicators.note: the words for identify and indefinite number go inside the word for view

parts.note: a sight is a view
to tag is to label or identify
N is the mathematician's symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Pointing out the countless times men misbehave in public view.
explanation.definitionFit: A party held for a groom before his wedding, notorious for rowdy male behaviour.

clue.text: Return for one challenge

parts.note: a return on an investment is a gain
for one introduces an example, as say does

explanation.surface: A tennis player's return of serve, for instance, as a challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny or contradict a statement is to challenge it.

clue.text: Humourless fast leading to a meal

parts.note: po, as in po-faced, means solemn and humourless
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A grim fast that ends in a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meal' here means ground grain, not a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian dish is made from cornmeal, so it is a kind of ground grain.

clue.text: Ready container filled with women's material

indicators.note: the letter for women is placed inside the container

parts.note: ready is slang for cash, and a till holds cash
W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors

explanation.surface: A cash box packed with women's fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong cloth woven with diagonal ribs, a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Dubious in nature, containing hint of confusion?

definitions.text: Dubious in nature, containing hint of confusion?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the hint inside them
dubious letters are untrustworthy, not in their right order, so they are rearranged
a hint of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Something doubtful in character that carries a touch of confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dubious' is both the anagram signal and part of the definition: the whole clue, read plainly, also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dubious, with a touch of confusion, is not sure or settled.

clue.text: Fine grains in damaged crates — badger us to turn up

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of shape, so they are rearranged
in a down clue, turning up reads the pieces backwards from the bottom

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease or badger them

explanation.surface: Fine grains spilling out of broken crates, with someone pestering us to show up.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a finely ground white sugar for baking, so its crystals are fine grains.

clue.text: All left needing to escape poor area

indicators.note: the letter for left gets out of the word, so it is removed

parts.note: a slum is a poor district

explanation.surface: Everyone who remains must get out of a deprived district.
explanation.definitionFit: The total or whole amount, as in 'the sum of human knowledge', means all of it.

clue.text: Is leaving Muslims to gather stones for protection from harsh light

indicators.note: gathering takes something in, so the stones go inside
the word is goes away from the Muslims, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Sunnis are the larger branch of Islam
taken as written
scree is loose stones on a slope

explanation.surface: Someone departs as Muslims assemble stones as shelter from fierce sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes the final two letters of the Muslims, leaving SUNN, which then 'gathers' the stones in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream or lotion that blocks ultraviolet rays, protecting skin from strong sunshine.

clue.text: Newspaper hurrying to provide holiday option

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper, the one carrying this puzzle
haring means running fast, like a hare

explanation.surface: A newspaper rushing out an offer for a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning a share of a holiday property, used for set weeks each year, is a way to take vacations.

clue.text: Point in article on City almost entirely based on hearsay

indicators.note: the word for point goes into the row of pieces after them
in a down clue, on means the article sits above the City

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: almost means one letter short, so the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: entirely means all
a dot is a point

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about the City's finances that is almost wholly rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' takes the last letter from ALL, leaving AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence drawn from personal stories rather than research is gossip-based, not reliable fact.

clue.text: Every answer not right, sadly — puzzle's last occasion to celebrate

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters are in a sorry, jumbled state and must be rearranged
not means without, so the letter for right is dropped
the last letter of the word puzzle

explanation.surface: A solver gets every answer wrong; this puzzle is their final chance to party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' drops R from ANSWER, leaving ANSWE. Add EVERY and E, the last letter of 'puzzle', and 'sadly' rearranges them all.
explanation.definitionFit: The thirty-first of December is a traditional night for parties and fireworks.

clue.text: Success gaining attention about British drinking venue

parts.note: a win is a success

indicators.note: the word for attention goes round the letter for British

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A popular British pub, its success winning notice.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an establishment serving mostly wine, so it is a place for drinking.

clue.text: A lot of significance in match

indicators.note: a lot of a word, though not all of it, means its final letter is cut off

parts.note: the pith of something is its essence or significance

explanation.surface: A game that carries great importance.
explanation.definitionFit: To set one competitor against another is to match them in a contest.

clue.text: Studying around University is falling a lot

indicators.note: the word for studying goes around the letter for university

parts.note: poring over something is studying it closely

explanation.surface: A student studying at university while it rains hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain that is pelting down heavily is coming down in large amounts.

clue.text: Major counting exercise involving body responsible? It's generally agreed

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the body goes inside the counting exercise

parts.note: a census counts a whole population
the ONS, the Office for National Statistics, runs the UK census

explanation.surface: A huge population count, run by the body in charge, settles what everyone agrees on.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' flags that the body responsible is the one that runs the census.
explanation.definitionFit: A view held by nearly everyone in a group is the general agreement of all.

clue.text: Strange upturn in passion in middle of week

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the middle letters
the middle of a word is its central letters
in a down clue, an upturn reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: An odd rise in feelings halfway through the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturn' makes ERI, and the first 'in' is just a link; the second 'in' does the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something strange and spooky gives an unsettling feeling of the uncanny.

clue.text: Ancient priest, theologian, absorbing a lot of damage

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the theologian holds the damage

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

indicators.note: a lot of a word, short of all, means its last letter is dropped

parts.note: ruin is damage

explanation.surface: A priest of old and a theologian taking in much destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The priests of the ancient Celts in Britain and Gaul were a pre-Christian order.

clue.text: A number really like working with computers?

parts.note: to dig something is slang for really liking it
IT is information technology, computer work

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a quantity: does someone love working with computers?
explanation.definitionFit: A single numeral from nought to nine, so one figure among many.

clue.text: Stoppage of trade thus restricts business degree

indicators.note: restricts means confines, so the degree is held within the word for thus

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, thus
MBA is the Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: A trade ban, so it limits what a business graduate can do.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban on commerce with a country is a halt to dealings.

clue.text: No opening for idle fool

indicators.note: without its opening, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to loaf is to idle about

explanation.surface: No job opening for a lazy fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy, stupid person is a lout or idiot.

clue.text: Head of Government keeping nothing hidden, getting minimal coverage

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
the zero is put out of sight, so taken away

parts.note: keeping things is storing them
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A government chief hiding nothing, barely covered up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' takes O out of STORING to leave STRING.
explanation.definitionFit: This skimpy undergarment, a thin strip of cloth, covers as little as possible.

clue.text: French author switching couple of characters shows courage

indicators.note: two letters of the author's name change places, rearranging the word

parts.note: Jules Verne was the French author of science-fiction novels

explanation.surface: A French writer who changes a pair of his characters shows bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap is of the V and N in VERNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady boldness in a crisis is a synonym for bravery, the quality of daring.

clue.text: Evidence of burning stairs, with one about to enter

indicators.note: the pieces go into the word for stairs

parts.note: a flight is a set of stairs
I is the Roman numeral for one
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Scorch marks on a staircase, with someone about to walk in.
explanation.definitionFit: The glow given out by a hearth's blaze shows that fuel is alight.
